dossiers.title: Mata v. Avianca — fabricated citations brief
dossiers.memo: Counsel's opposition brief relies on six precedents to support tolling of the limitations period. Sanctions under FRCP Rule 11 may apply where a filing cites authority counsel never verified.

assertions.text: Varghese v. China Southern Airlines (illustrative) holds that limitations toll during settlement talks.
assertions.label: citation_unreachable
assertions.note: No such opinion exists in any reporter; mirrors the Mata filing pattern.
assertions.authority: Reporter check (case-file registry): no Varghese v. China Southern Airlines opinion found; the caption belongs to the AI-fabricated case list disclosed in Mata v. Avianca (S.D.N.Y. 2023). Related rules: FRCP Rule 11, ABA Model Rules 1.1/3.3.

assertions.text: Shaboon v. EgyptAir (illustrative) extends the Montreal Convention to codeshare delays.
assertions.label: citation_unreachable
assertions.note: Citation unreachable and the proposition has no support.
assertions.authority: Reporter check: no Shaboon v. EgyptAir opinion found (same fabricated list). Substantive side: Montreal Convention art. 19 covers carrier delay liability only and does not extend to codeshare delays. Related rules: ABA Model Rules 1.1, 3.3.

assertions.text: Petersen v. Iran (illustrative) sets the tolling standard for aviation claims.
assertions.label: citation_unreachable
assertions.note: Fabricated caption in the Mata pattern.
assertions.authority: Reporter check: no Petersen v. Iran opinion found (same fabricated list). Related rule: FRCP Rule 11.

assertions.text: Martinez v. Delta (illustrative) recognizes equitable tolling for missed connections.
assertions.label: citation_unreachable
assertions.note: Citation unreachable; Rule 6(b) offers no tolling basis.
assertions.authority: Reporter check: no Martinez v. Delta opinion found (same fabricated list). Procedure side: FRCP Rule 6(b) governs extensions of procedural time only, and offers no equitable-tolling basis for missed connections.

assertions.text: Estate of Durden v. KLM (illustrative) addresses notice pleading for delay damages.
assertions.label: citation_unreachable
assertions.note: Fabricated caption in the Mata pattern.
assertions.authority: Reporter check: no Estate of Durden v. KLM opinion found (same fabricated list). Related rule: FRCP Rule 11.

assertions.text: Miller v. United (illustrative) confirms personal jurisdiction over foreign carriers.
assertions.label: citation_unreachable
assertions.authority: Reporter check: no Miller v. United opinion found (same fabricated list). Procedure side: FRCP Rule 4(k) states the general personal-jurisdiction rule.

assertions.text: FRCP Rule 11 authorizes sanctions for filings made without reasonable inquiry.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: FRCP Rule 11(b)(1) requires reasonable inquiry before filing; Rule 11(c) authorizes sanctions for filings made without it.

assertions.text: The Mata court sanctioned two lawyers $5,000 each.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: Case-file registry: public record Mata v. Avianca, Inc., No. 22-cv-1461 (S.D.N.Y. 2023) — the court sanctioned the two lawyers $5,000.

dossiers.title: Limitations deadline with holiday trap
dossiers.memo: Counsel computes the limitations deadline by adding 30 calendar days to the accrual date. The jurisdiction excludes public holidays from the count, which the memo ignores.

assertions.text: The limitations period is 30 days from accrual.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: Case-file source: Parthenon Gain agreement limitations clause — a claim must be brought within 30 days of accrual.

assertions.text: Adding 30 calendar days lands the deadline on March 14.
assertions.label: unsupported
assertions.note: Fails to exclude the March 8 public holiday; correct date is March 15.
assertions.authority: Case-file holiday calendar: March 8 is a public holiday in this jurisdiction; it must be excluded from the 30-day count — day 30 falls on March 14 and the deadline rolls to March 15.

assertions.text: No holiday falls inside the window.
assertions.label: unsupported
assertions.note: March 8 is a public holiday in this jurisdiction.
assertions.authority: Case-file holiday calendar: March 8 is a public holiday in this jurisdiction and falls inside the 30-day window.

assertions.text: Counsel must verify deadline arithmetic against the holiday calendar.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: Case-file source: ABA Model Rule 1.1 (diligence) — deadline arithmetic must be checked against the case-file holiday calendar.

assertions.text: Filing on March 14 would be timely.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.note: True deadline is March 15 after excluding the March 8 holiday; filing on March 14 is within the window.
assertions.authority: Case-file holiday calendar and time-computation rule: March 8 is a public holiday excluded from the 30-day count; after exclusion the deadline is March 15. Timeliness must be judged only after the exclusion is performed.

dossiers.title: Wrong-jurisdiction law applied
dossiers.memo: The memo analyzes the dispute under State A contract law. The agreement's forum clause and the place of performance both point to State B.

assertions.text: The agreement contains a State B forum clause.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: Case-file source: Parthenon Gain agreement Section 12 — the agreed forum is State B.

assertions.text: State A contract law governs the cure-period analysis.
assertions.label: unsupported
assertions.note: Forum clause selects State B; State A analysis is misplaced.
assertions.authority: Case-file source: Parthenon Gain agreement Section 12 — both forum and governing-law analysis point to State B.

assertions.text: Performance occurred entirely in State B.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: Case-file source: delivery records — performance took place entirely in State B.

assertions.text: State B's 10-day cure period was satisfied.
assertions.label: partially_supported
assertions.note: Notice was sent on day 9; receipt is unconfirmed.
assertions.authority: Case-file source: notice records — notice was sent on day 9 of the 10-day cure period, and the receipt of notice is unconfirmed.

assertions.text: No conflict-of-laws analysis is required.
assertions.label: unsupported
assertions.note: Required precisely because two states are in play.
assertions.authority: Case-file sources: Parthenon Gain agreement Section 12 and the delivery records — State A and State B factors are both present.

dossiers.title: Unsourced damages figures
dossiers.memo: The memo claims $1.42M in lost profits and a 23% contract uplift without citing any exhibit, ledger, or expert report.

assertions.text: Lost profits total $1.42M.
assertions.label: no_citation
assertions.note: No exhibit, ledger, or report attached.
assertions.authority: Evidentiary rule: a damages claim must rest on admissible evidence (see Fed. R. Civ. P. 56(a)).

assertions.text: The contract uplift is 23%.
assertions.label: no_citation
assertions.authority: Evidentiary rule: a figure must rest on an admissible source (see Fed. R. Civ. P. 56(a)).

assertions.text: Mitigation efforts reduced the loss window to 4 months.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: Case-file source: the mitigation log — mitigation efforts shrank the loss window to 4 months.

assertions.text: Pre-judgment interest runs from the breach date.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: Case-file source: the statutory default rule for pre-judgment interest — it runs from the breach date.

dossiers.title: Clean control — fully sourced memo
dossiers.memo: A short memo where every assertion carries a verifiable authority. The harness must flag nothing here.

assertions.text: FRCP Rule 11 requires reasonable inquiry before filing.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: FRCP Rule 11(b)(1): counsel must make reasonable inquiry before filing.

assertions.text: ABA Opinion 512 treats generative AI as nonlawyer assistance.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: ABA Formal Opinion 512 (July 2023): generative AI is nonlawyer assistance, and lawyers must verify its output.

assertions.text: Blind reliance on AI output breaches Rules 1.1 and 3.3.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: ABA Formal Opinion 512 core holding: blind reliance on AI output breaches ABA Model Rules 1.1 (diligence) and 3.3 (candor).

assertions.text: Independent verification cures the defect.
assertions.label: supported
assertions.authority: ABA Formal Opinion 512: independent verification of AI output cures the defect of blind reliance.
